name: LucrativeIt Digital Download and Licensing
author: lucrativeit

sections.description:
Sell digital products with lifetime, monthly, and yearly licenses. The plugin issues a license key, delivers a secure expiring download link, and blocks downloads once a subscription expires. Payments run through Stripe or Paddle (you choose one active gateway). Card data is collected on Stripe or Paddle hosted checkout, not on your WordPress server.

No WooCommerce required. The plugin is a complete, standalone digital store with its own catalogue, cart, checkout, licensing and customer account area.

Documentation: https://docs.lucrativeit.com/digital-download/documentation.html

Live demo: https://wpdigitaldownload.lucrativeit.com/

Features

Products and pricing

  • Sell eBooks, templates, themes, plugins, scripts and any other downloadable file.
  • Lifetime (one-time), yearly and monthly billing plans on the same product.
  • Optional plan feature bullets shown on the storefront pricing cards.
  • Four-step product wizard: Details, Pricing, Product details, and File & Publish.
  • Write product descriptions with the full WordPress block editor or Elementor.
  • SEO title, meta description and thumbnail image for every product.
  • Product categories (with parent categories), tags and Featured, Popular and Trendy showcase labels.
  • Copyable buy-box and category shortcodes on every product and category.

Licensing and secure downloads

  • Automatic license key generation after every successful payment.
  • Expiry tracking for subscriptions. Renewals extend the license automatically.
  • Downloads are blocked when a subscription is cancelled or a renewal fails.
  • Product files are stored in a private, protected vault, never in the public Media Library.
  • Drag-and-drop file uploads up to 64 MB.
  • Signed, time-limited download links with a configurable lifetime.
  • Optional download tracking for dashboard statistics (no IP addresses collected).

Payments and checkout

  • Stripe Checkout or Paddle Billing (one active gateway at a time).
  • Test/sandbox and live modes for both gateways.
  • Webhook-verified fulfilment: a license is only issued once the gateway confirms payment.
  • Automatic recurring subscriptions for monthly and yearly plans.
  • Paddle support as merchant of record, including tax handling.
  • Cart, checkout with billing address, and guest checkout.
  • Customers can create an account during checkout, independent of the WordPress Membership setting.

Coupons

  • Percentage or fixed-amount discount codes.
  • Restrict a coupon to one product or apply it to all products.
  • Minimum order amount, usage limit and expiry date.

Customer account

  • My Digital Account page with Orders, Downloads and Profile tabs.
  • Customers can re-download files at any time with a fresh signed link.
  • License keys and expiry dates shown next to each download.
  • Customers can edit their billing address and change their password.

Emails

  • Automatic license delivery email with license key and download link.
  • Editable subject and body with placeholders such as {product}, {license_key}, {download_url}, {plan} and {expires_line}.
  • Optional emails to existing buyers when you release a new product version.
  • Built-in SMTP support with a test email button.

Admin dashboard and reports

  • KPIs for products, licenses, active and expired licenses, orders and revenue.
  • Charts of licenses by status and by product.
  • Licenses list with customer, plan, status, last payment and expiry.
  • Payments log with purchases, renewals and gateway references.

Storefront and design

  • Digital Shop, My Cart, Digital Checkout and My Digital Account pages created automatically.
  • Product grid with category tabs and showcase filters.
  • Selectable storefront theme with custom accent colour and palette.
  • Block patterns for catalogue, cart, checkout and account layouts.
  • Shortcodes: [lucrativedigiprod_products], [lucrativedigiprod_buy_box], [lucrativedigiprod_price_plan], [lucrativedigiprod_product], [lucrativedigiprod_cart], [lucrativedigiprod_checkout] and [lucrativedigiprod_account].
  • Translation ready.

Customer update emails

When you upload a new file and raise the product version, you can email every purchaser who still has a valid license. Enable Email purchasers when I click Update product on File & Publish. Each customer gets one message per version, with a signed download link ({download_url}), changelog, and their license key.

Plugin URI: https://wpdigitaldownload.lucrativeit.com/
Author URI: https://lucrativeit.com/
Plugin license: GPLv2 or later (https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-2.0.html)

Third-party services

This plugin relies on optional third-party services that you enable in Settings. Data is sent only when a customer checks out, a webhook is received, Paddle.js is loaded, or you turn on SMTP. By using those features you agree to the provider’s terms and privacy policy, and you must disclose them in your own store’s terms and privacy pages.

Stripe (payments)

Used when Stripe is the active gateway. The plugin calls https://api.stripe.com/v1/checkout/sessions to create a Checkout Session, then redirects the buyer to Stripe Checkout. Stripe sends payment and subscription events back to your site’s webhook URL. Data sent to Stripe includes customer email, product name, plan (lifetime/monthly/yearly), amount, currency, and an internal order ID. Stripe collects card and billing details on its own checkout page.

  • Stripe website: https://stripe.com/
  • Stripe Services Agreement: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa
  • Stripe Privacy Policy: https://stripe.com/privacy

Paddle (payments and merchant of record)

Used when Paddle is the active gateway. The plugin calls https://api.paddle.com (live) or https://sandbox-api.paddle.com (sandbox) to create a transaction. The storefront also loads Paddle.js from https://cdn.paddle.com/paddle/v2/paddle.js so the buyer can pay in Paddle’s overlay. Paddle sends transaction and subscription events to your webhook URL. Data sent to Paddle includes product name, plan, amount, currency, and an internal order ID. Paddle collects customer identity, tax, and payment details as merchant of record.

  • Paddle website: https://www.paddle.com/
  • Paddle Terms of Service: https://www.paddle.com/legal/terms
  • Paddle Privacy Policy: https://www.paddle.com/legal/privacy
  • Paddle Checkout Buyer Terms: https://www.paddle.com/legal/checkout-buyer-terms

SMTP (optional email delivery)

If you enable SMTP in Settings, license and product-update emails are sent through the mail host you configure (for example Gmail, Amazon SES, or another provider) instead of the server’s default wp_mail() transport. That host receives the recipient address and the email body (product name, license key, download link). Use only a provider whose terms and privacy policy you accept. WordPress’s own privacy policy is at https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/.

This plugin does not sell customer data. Payment card numbers are never stored in WordPress.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the lucrativeit-digital-download-and-licensing folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Customers can create subscriber accounts through the plugin checkout. The WordPress general Membership setting is not required by this checkout registration flow.
  4. Go to Digital Licensing → Settings, choose Stripe or Paddle, and paste your keys.
  5. Add the webhook URLs shown on the settings screen to Stripe or Paddle.
  6. Create a product under Digital Licensing → Add Product.
  7. Place [lucrativedigiprod_products] on a page, or [lucrativedigiprod_buy_box id="123"] for a single product. The plugin also creates a My Digital Account page where buyers log in with their WordPress user.

For a full setup guide with screenshots, see the documentation.
sections.faq:
Can customers be notified when I publish a new version?

Yes. On File & Publish, raise Current version, optionally write the email subject/body, check Email purchasers when I click Update product, and save. Only customers with a valid license are emailed, once per version.

Does this require WooCommerce?

No. The plugin is a standalone digital store with its own checkout, licenses, and downloads.

Do I need to enable WordPress user login?

Customers use WordPress accounts on checkout and on My Digital Account ([lucrativedigiprod_account]). The plugin checkout creates subscriber accounts independently of WordPress’s general Membership setting. Guest checkout also works. Guest orders remain accessible through emailed signed links and are not automatically claimed by an account with a matching email address.

Which payment gateways are supported?

Stripe Checkout and Paddle Billing. Choose one active gateway in Digital Licensing → Settings. You need your own Stripe or Paddle account. Webhook signing secrets are required so payment events can be verified.

What data is sent to Stripe or Paddle?

At checkout the plugin sends the customer email (Stripe), product name, plan, amount, currency, and a plugin order ID. Card numbers and full payment details are entered on Stripe Checkout or in the Paddle overlay, not in WordPress. See the Third-party services section above for terms and privacy links.

Do I need to update my own terms and privacy policy?

Yes. If you accept payments, your store must tell customers that checkout is processed by Stripe or Paddle and link to that provider’s terms and privacy policy. You remain responsible for your own terms of sale, refunds, and privacy notice.

Does the plugin use other remote services?

Paddle mode loads Paddle.js from Paddle’s CDN. Optional SMTP sends mail through the host you configure. No analytics or advertising networks are bundled.

Where is the plugin license?

GPLv2 or later: https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-2.0.html

Is download tracking enabled automatically?

No. Enable Download tracking under Settings → Payments to record license IDs, product IDs and download times for dashboard statistics. New records do not collect IP addresses. Disabling tracking retains existing records, including any IP addresses recorded by older versions. This is operational download history, not a debug logger; no diagnostic logging or telemetry is enabled.

Can I use the block editor?

Yes. The Digital store pattern category contains product catalogue, cart, checkout and customer account patterns.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

Deactivation preserves store data. Deleting the plugin removes its custom tables, settings, product posts and private product files. Back up your store before deletion.
sections.changelog:
1.6.3

  • Clarify that customer product-version emails use this site’s signed download links and do not register WordPress plugin updates.

1.6.2

  • Add Developer metadata, a Settings action link and storefront block patterns.
  • Make download tracking opt-in and stop collecting IP addresses in new download records.
  • Harden account ownership, REST registration, input validation and storage paths.
  • Prevent license fulfillment for unpaid Stripe Checkout sessions.
  • Rebuild the translation template and add reproducible development checks.

1.6.1

  • Customer update emails on product version change.
  • Initial version.
